title: Ordered grip-trial decline does not improve walking-limitation prediction beyond peak strength: a two-cycle NHANES test
abstract: Peak handgrip measures discard trial order. We tested whether bilateral first-to-third-trial decline, divided by summed hand maxima, improves prediction of concurrent quarter-mile walking difficulty beyond peak strength, asymmetry, age, sex and body size. A survey-weighted logistic model fitted in 1150 adults aged60+ from NHANES2011–2012 was transferred without recalibration to 1237 separately recruited adults in2013–2014. Brier score rose from 0.133559 to 0.133881 (delta+0.000322; approximate target-PSU95% interval-0.000119 to+0.000727; joint training/target interval-0.000544 to+0.003441). AUC changed by-0.001857. Flexible baselines, maximal-effort and no-pain restrictions did not rescue the primary finding; an older subgroup and unweighted fitting changed its sign. This prespecified negative representation test does not establish absence of neuromuscular information. Completion and questionnaire routing exclude many disabled adults, and survey-cycle transfer is not independent clinical-cohort validation.
